text:
maya: Heads-up — I hit a weird interaction between per-tier routing priority and A/B rollouts during the Canary earlier.

sam: quick summary? what happened exactly?

maya: We had tier=enterprise preempt set to true so enterprise traffic can steal capacity from standard. During A/B rollout we expected a 10% exposure for variant B, but enterprise traffic bumped B to ~30% because preemption moved requests to nodes where B was serving.

cheng: 😬 that sounds like routing priority should be orthogonal to rollout exposure. We didn’t intend preemption to change sample weights.

maya: Agreed. The rollout config had "scope: per-tier" and we interpreted it as "slice by tier then sample". The runtime currently applies routing first (so priority+preemption) then sampling.

dalia: So current pipeline = smart-routing -> capacity assignment -> variant selection? That order would explain it.

sam: Can we reorder to do variant selection before preemption? I worry about latency/cost implications if we start sampling before routing.

ben: Implementation note: if we sample first, we need to guarantee placement for sampled requests, or we might need to fallback if sampled variant has no capacity in that region/tier. That adds complexity.

irina: Also telemetry: dashboards currently show per-tier rollout % based on accepted requests at the node level, not the initial sample intent. We need a metric that captures intended exposure vs actual exposure post-routing.

maya: Exactly — ops saw the post-routing metric and rolled back the rollout thinking the config was wrong. Intent was fine, runtime behaviour caused skew.

rollouts-bot: deploy-event: rollout "chat-v2-b" started (10% global, per-tier scoping). Canary window: 30m.

sam: Two potential fixes: 1) make sampling happen pre-routing (store intent in request context), then route but treat intent as sticky and don't preempt it away; 2) keep routing-first but add a reservation step for sampled requests so preemption respects reserved capacity.

cheng: Option 1 seems cleaner conceptually: sample -> tag request with variant -> route with a policy that honors tags when possible. But we need to decide tie-breaker: if tagged variant has zero compatible nodes, fallback to a compatible variant immediately.

ben: Tie-breaker idea: add a small TTL reservation token. When a request is sampled for variant B, we attempt to reserve capacity on a compatible node for X ms. If reservation fails, mark request as "fallback-eligible" and run fallback logic. That avoids changing global preemption semantics too much.

dalia: That reservation path will add RPCs to the scheduler though. We should measure overhead. Any microbenchmarks?

maya: I ran a quick sim locally: reservation-first added ~1.5ms median p99 0.7ms overhead under normal load. Worth it if it prevents exposure skew.

irina: For dashboards we need these new metrics: "intended_exposure_by_scope", "actual_exposure_post_routing", and "reservation_fail_rate". Also a small panel showing per-tier delta (actual - intended).

sam: API debate: do we expose a rollout flag like `honor_sampling_before_preemption: true|false` in the rollout config, or should this be automatic when scope=per-tier?

cheng: I vote for automatic: if scope=per-tier and preemption=true, default to honoring sampling to match user mental model. Allow override for advanced users. Document clearly.

ben: Edge-case: cross-region constraints. If scope=region+tier and variant pinned to a region, sampling-first may still fail due to soft-affinity. Need clear fallback semantics: fallback to nearest compatible variant in same region, else degrade to global fallback and log.

maya: Also we need to think about quotas. A sampled request that gets preempted away might still count against user quota in current accounting. We should count quota at intent time, not after routing, otherwise quotas get gamed by preemption.

irina: Good call. Update quota docs and console to show "quota impact = intended requests" vs "fulfilled requests". Add a flag in telemetry export so billing team can reconcile.

dalia: UX in Console: when users configure A/B with per-tier scope, show a callout: "Routing priority/preemption may affect actual exposure. We will attempt to honor sampling; you can toggle strict reservation for lower variance (may increase latency)." Include example diagrams.

sam: Security question: any risk of reservation tokens being replayed to game exposure? Tokens should be single-use and short-lived and tied to request nonce.

ben: Yes single-use + HMAC with request-id will be fine. Scheduler must validate.

cheng: Action items:
- cheng + ben: prototype reservation token flow and measure latency/overhead (1d).
- maya: run a replay sim on last week's production traces to estimate exposure skew (today).
- irina: add telemetry metrics to the eval dashboard and a draft console callout (2d).
- sam: draft API wording for rollout flag and default behavior (1d).

maya: I'll also put a short note in the Canary runbook about checking intended vs actual exposure and when to roll back.

dalia: 👍 canary team will be on standby for the next run.

sam: Thanks — seems like a solid plan. If someone wants to pair after lunch, ping me.

irina: one more: add an alert if delta(actual,intended) > 5% for >5min during canary windows.

ben: noted. I'll add the alert prototype to the observability repo.

maya: closing loop: tagging this thread for follow-ups. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
